items.title: Senior Research Associate: Accelerating Scientific Discovery in the Age of GenAI (1326-26)
items.description:
The  Mathematical AI for Decision and Discovery (MADD)  group at Lancaster University is recruiting postdoctoral researchers, funded by Dr Henry Moss’s UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship. These long-term posts run until November 2030 and come with a generous budget for conference travel and extended research visits to the group’s international collaborators.   About the role  In drug discovery, materials science and engineering design, every experiment is expensive. Bayesian optimisation and experimental design help choose which experiments to run, but they struggle when designs must meet complex, domain-specific feasibility requirements. MADD turns generative AI models, trained on known feasible designs, into rigorous decision rules for real experimental campaigns.  You will lead work in one or more of our research strands:   Gaussian process flows: probabilistic models that can be conditioned on almost any form of real-world knowledge, used as richer surrogates in experimental design.  Generative-AI-driven experimental design: theory and methods for Bayesian optimisation when candidates come from generative models.  Fine-grained control of generative models: steering pre-trained models to meet precise campaign criteria without costly retraining.   You will also publish at top venues; help shape the group’s open-source Python library; lead a flagship application with an industrial partner (e.g. drug discovery, protein engineering, fusion energy, sustainable aviation or hardware design); co-supervise PhD students; and mentor junior researchers.  These are full-time, fixed-term positions until November 2030. Flexible working arrangements will be considered, but you will be expected to be present on the Lancaster campus a minimum of two days per week.   What we’re looking for  A PhD in machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field, with a strong publication record in Bayesian optimisation, experimental design, Gaussian processes, probabilistic modelling, or deep generative modelling. We welcome both theory-focused candidates and those experienced in building large generative models. Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or JAX are expected.  We particularly welcome applications from women and other groups underrepresented in the mathematical sciences and AI.   Travel, visits and collaboration  External collaboration is at the heart of MADD. Each year you will receive funding for an extended research visit to a partner, attendance at major international conferences, regular visits to UK industrial partners, and external training.   Find out more  Informal enquiries to Dr Henry Moss ( h.moss@lancaster.ac.uk ) are strongly encouraged. More about the group:  https://henrymoss.github.io/ .

items.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Mathematical Physics (Senior Research Associate) (1286-26)
items.description:
Lancaster University’s School of Physics and Astronomy is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate (Senior Research Associate) as part of the John Templeton Foundation award “Open Quantum Systems  and the Causal Structure of Reality”.   The Open Systems collaboration will apply formal, physical and conceptional innovations from the study of open quantum systems to systems without fixed causal structure. Quantum models of the universe feature non-fixed causal structure in terms of dynamical and, in some cases, emergent spacetime structure. Quantum cosmology offers the most general and challenging arena for the open systems approach to physics and metaphysics, since the standard assumption is that the universe is subject to closed quantum dynamics. Fundamental reality is standardly understood by philosophers and scientists to be whatever provides the basis for everything.  The Postdoctoral Research Associate will lead their own research program, and be encouraged to work in this area on issues regarding general relativity and cosmology contributing to questions of the role of scale in general relativity, the emergence of temporal structure, the use of quantum reference frames or other related issues.   The Postdoctoral Research Associate post is full time, funded for 24 months from 1 st  July 2027. In conjunction with the standard application process, please upload a CV and also a writing sample of either a) your best published work or b) single thesis chapter (in the latter case, 30 pages maximum inclusive of references) with your application.  If you have any queries regarding this position, please contact David Sloan at d.sloan@lancaster.ac.uk

items.title: Senior Research Associate in Infectious Disease Epidemiology (1224-26)
items.description:
We are seeking to appoint a full-time Research Associate or Senior Research Associate  until March 2029, with the possibility of further extension.  This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing research programme using real-world contact data and mathematical modelling to understand how infectious diseases spread and the potential impact of different control measures. The work will focus predominantly on two uniquely rich datasets, one capturing general population contact patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic using large-scale contact tracing data, and one focused specifically on school-aged children, to help shape public health policy on disease control both in schools and more broadly. The successful candidate will join Lancaster Medical School and work closely with Dr Jonathan Read and Dr Trystan Leng.  We welcome applications from researchers with a PhD in (or equivalent experience) in infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical modelling, quantitative social science, or a related discipline. The postholder will clean and analyse contact patterns from two distinct datasets: 1) the NHS/UKHSA contact tracing data from England, collected during the COVID-19 pandemic and 2) data collected from the School and Community Connections study, a bespoke study which will collect data specifically for this analysis, aimed at understanding the contact patterns of schoolchildren. Further, the postholder will use transmission-dynamic models informed by this contact data alongside surveillance data, fitted using Bayesian methods, to undertake scenario-based mathematical modelling of the potential impact of a range of public health interventions, as well as exploring the usefulness of contact data in explaining observed patterns of incidence.  Depending on experience, the postholder may also contribute to survey design and data collection during the School and Community Connections Study.  The post is funded jointly through a MRC grant awarded to Dr Read and through Dr Leng's Wellcome Early Career Award 'Control without closure: school-level approaches for pathogen control within and between schools':  https://wellcome.org/research-funding/funding-portfolio/funded-grants/control-without-closure-school-level-approaches   You will liaise with colleagues within Lancaster Medical School (Dr Sam Moore) alongside external partners, including Prof Henrik Salje (University of Cambridge), Prof Moritz Kraemer (University of Oxford), colleagues at UKHSA, and the UK government’s Department for Education science team.  You will be expected to be based at Lancaster University, however, we can consider remote working within the UK. There is also the opportunity for a longer-term research visit to external partners’ institutions.  We welcome applications from candidates seeking flexible working requests.  You will join a top 10-UK university in the Complete University Guide 2027 situated in a vibrant research environment. Lancaster Medical School, within the Faculty of Health and Medicine (FHM) at Lancaster University, provides a friendly research environment that strongly supports the individual needs of each employee and which actively promotes a healthy work-life balance. FHM is committed to family-friendly and flexible working policies and has held a Silver Athena SWAN award since 2014 in recognition of its good employment practice undertaken to address gender equality in higher education and research.  For more information, please contact:  Dr Jonathan Read:  Jonathan.read@lancaster.ac.uk   Dr Trystan Leng,  t.leng@lancaster.ac.uk   The post is available from 1 st  January 2027.

items.title: Senior Research Associate (1137-26)
items.description:
The School of Mathematical Sciences at Lancaster University invites applications for a three-year postdoctoral position to work on the EPSRC-funded project  “ Mutations and geometric models”. The Principal Investigator is Dr Coelho Simões.   Calabi-Yau (CY) triangulated categories are ubiquitous in mathematics, particularly in geometry and representation theory. Due to their physical origin, n-CY categories have been extensively studied for n=2,3. However, as a homological condition, the n-CY property can be studied for any integer n meaning there are many more examples: categories naturally arising in modular representation theory, singularity theory, Fuss-Catalan combinatorics, and higher homological algebra are n-CY for n different from 2 and 3. The systematic study of CY categories in these wider contexts is in its infancy and many aspects remain poorly understood. The main aim of the project seeks to provide methods to address this shortfall using mutations and geometric models.  The successful candidate is expected to hold a PhD degree in mathematics or a related discipline, with specialism in one of the fields of homological algebra, representation theory or algebraic combinatorics. Expertise in triangulated categories, representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras, combinatorial/geometric models arising from surfaces, singularity theory or modular representation theory is highly desirable. You will be expected to learn quickly, engage with new ideas, and contribute new insights.  This work will take place in our thriving Pure Mathematics section, which has considerable expertise in algebra, geometry, analysis, probability, and discrete mathematics. Lancaster is one of the UK’s top mathematical science departments, ranked 7th in the most recent Research Excellence Framework, and joint 1st for the impact of its research. The School, which holds an Athena SWAN Bronze Award, strives to provide a supportive and friendly environment for early career researchers, and offers a comprehensive career development programme. You will be able to focus on your research as the post carries no teaching or administrative duties. Teaching experience will be available on a voluntary basis should you wish to gain teaching experience. You will be encouraged to conduct research visits and will have access to travel funds to do so.   The position starts on 1st February 2027 (or as soon as possible after), for up to 36 months. When applying, in addition to completing the online application, candidates should attach a full CV, a cover letter, a 1-page research statement describing how your expertise is relevant to this position and your future research plans, and the details of two referees. Interviews will take place in December and will be conducted online.  Please contact Dr Raquel Coelho Simões (   r.coelhosimoes@lancaster.ac.uk ) for further information or to discuss the post informally.

items.title: Research Fellow in Additive Semiconductor Device Fabrication (057926)
items.description:
The role   We seek a Research Fellow in Thin-Film Device and Circuit Fabrication to contribute to EPSRC project EP/Y000196/1. The appointment is part-time (0.5 FTE), with significant flexibility to adapt the working fraction and working pattern to the successful candidate's circumstances and the needs of the project. The post should start as soon as practicable and is expected to run until the end of July 2027.  The Researcher will undertake strongly experimental and data-intensive research on advanced multi-gate thin-film transistor structures. The work will involve fabrication using a variety of semiconductor and insulator materials, systematic electrical characterisation of large device arrays, automated measurement, and rapid analysis of device and circuit parameters. Particular emphasis will be placed on source-gated transistors (SGTs), multimodal transistors (MMTs), printing and dispensing processes, and rigorous extraction and interpretation of geometrical and electrical statistics.  About You  The successful candidate will have a PhD, or current progress towards a PhD, in Electronic Engineering or a closely related discipline with proven hands-on experience operating the XTPL Delta printer, including material selection, optimization of printing parameters for feature size and fill generation, remote operation, and maintenance routine. They will also have a deep understanding of the fabrication, operation, optimisation, and key performance indicators of source-gated transistors (SGTs) and multimodal transistors (MMTs). They would also have practical experience in thin-film device fabrication, including evaporation, dispensing, and printing, across relevant semiconductor and insulator material systems.   Additional Background Information   You will join a collaborative research team at the Advanced Technology Institute (ATI), University of Surrey, working on EPSRC project EP/Y000196/1. The role is strongly hands-on and data-intensive, with a particular emphasis on advanced thin-film transistor fabrication, automated characterisation, and rigorous analysis of large experimental datasets. Working with Dr Radu Sporea, you will interact closely with researchers and students contributing to related device, circuit, and technology-development activities.  Alongside the core experimental programme, the post holder will be expected to contribute to publication and presentation of research results, proposal development, and, where required, IP, commercialisation, technology transfer, and public engagement. Significant interaction with project partners is expected, and the role may involve national and international travel for collaborative experiments, analysis, and dissemination.  The University of Surrey is a research-intensive university based in Guildford. The Advanced Technology Institute is a multidisciplinary research environment spanning nanotechnology, energy, and large-area electronics, with specialist facilities supporting device fabrication and characterisation.  The University is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion. Research staff are supported in their career development through mentoring, training, and a collegial research environment in which varied skills and perspectives are valued.   How to Apply   Please submit your CV and cover letter with your application on the University website.   Please contact Dr Sporea for all enquiries:  r.a.sporea@surrey.ac.uk

items.title: Research Fellow in Quantum Electronic Structure Theory (3559026EB)
items.description:
We are seeking a highly motivated Research Fellow in the field of theoretical chemistry or physics to develop electronic structure theory for quantum dynamics on classic and quantum computers.   The successful candidate will be based at the University of Southampton (UK) in the group of Dr Karl Michael Ziems ( ziemsgroup.org ). The project includes collaborations with Prof Sonia Coriani at the Technical University of Denmark, Dr Erik Kjellgren at the University of Southern Denmark, and Prof Basile Curchod at the University of Bristol.  The position is funded for 3 years with an anticipated start date of the 1 st  of February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.    Project idea:    Understanding how molecules behave after photoexcitation is key to explaining fundamental processes in chemistry, physics, and biology. Simulating these processes requires accurate descriptions of the underlying electronic states, posing major challenges for computational methods. The emergence of quantum computing offers exciting opportunities to rethink established approaches and develop new theoretical tools bridging classical and quantum computing.  You will join a dynamic and collaborative research group working on electronic structure theory for classical and quantum computers, excited-state molecular dynamics, and quantum computing experiments. Our research combines fundamental method development with computational applications and collaborations with quantum start-ups, industry partners, and experimentalists studying ultrafast molecular processes.   Your research will focus on developing wavefunction-based electronic structure methods for excited-state molecular dynamics, applicable to both classical and quantum computers.  Possible directions include ground- and excited-state molecular gradients and nonadiabatic couplings, using both wavefunction and response theory formalisms. Depending on your interests and expertise, you can focus on classical or quantum computing, algorithm development, benchmarking, or experiments on quantum hardware. You will co-lead this project, co-supervise a PhD student, and work closely with experienced researchers and your supervisor, combining mathematical theory, scientific programming, and computational simulations.  A research stay in Denmark is possible through above collaborations.   Your background:   We welcome applicants from diverse scientific backgrounds. Essential strengths include programming (preferably Python), solid mathematical foundations, method development, and experience in wave function-based electronic structure theory. Experience in method development in 2 nd  quantization, computational chemistry, quantum dynamics, or quantum computing is advantageous.  Apply with your CV and by answering the short-listing question that are designed to evaluate your fit for the role.   For additional information or informal enquiries please email  K.M.Ziems@soton.ac.uk .

items.title: Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (VirION) (3554226BJ)
items.description:
We are seeking a proactive, highly motivated, and collaborative PhD candidate with a strong interest in virus-host interactions, cell biology and cellular metabolism. The project will identify small molecules that regulate peroxisome function and dynamics and determine how these compounds influence viral infection and host antiviral responses. The candidate will work at the interface of virology, peroxisome biology, chemical biology, and cell metabolism, using approaches such as mammalian cell culture, viral infection assays, small-molecule screening, molecular and biochemical techniques, quantitative image analysis, and advanced fluorescence and live-cell imaging. Previous hands-on experience with mammalian cell culture is strongly preferred, imaging or virological techniques experience is advantageous. The successful candidate should be enthusiastic about learning unfamiliar methods, analyzing complex datasets, and contributing actively to a collaborative, international, and interdisciplinary research network.   Essential Requirements:    Master’s degree or equivalent in biomedical sciences, molecular or cell biology, biochemistry, virology, chemical biology or a related discipline.  Experience with mammalian cell culture and molecular, cell biological, biochemical and molecular genetics techniques.  Experience with fluorescence or live-cell microscopy, quantitative image analysis, small-molecule or phenotypic screening, and virological techniques.  Excellent experimental and analytical skills; an organized, flexible and critical approach; the ability to work independently and collaboratively.  Excellent written and spoken English communication skills. Official proof of English-language proficiency is required.   For more details please check VirION’s webpage:  www.virion-msca.eu   Important: This position involves two separate application processes. Compulsory national service and/or short stays such as holidays are not taken into account. At the time of recruitment, you must not yet have been awarded your doctorate. We are looking for someone who can work confidently with large and varied single-cell datasets, and who enjoys developing, benchmarking, and testing new analytical approaches.  Experience in single-cell bioinformatics, containerisation, and workflow development will be critical to the role, and we are interested in your ability to think clearly, learn new methods, and work well with others. items.title: Research Fellow in Polar Oceanography (3550926HN)
items.description:
We are seeking an enthusiastic Research Fellow to join our vibrant research community at the National Oceanography Centre Southampton, University of Southampton, to work on the European Research Council-funded ROSS-SHIFT (Ross Sea Regime Shift) project.  The successful candidate will investigate potential regime shifts in ocean circulation in the Ross Sea and wider Southern Ocean, and their implications for Antarctic Ice Sheet melting and the Southern Ocean Overturning Circulation. The research will aim to improve our understanding of how changes in ocean circulation and freshwater content influence ocean heat transport towards Antarctic ice shelves, affect their basal melting, and interact with the large-scale overturning circulation. The work will involve the analysis of satellite observations, alongside in situ oceanographic measurements and numerical model outputs, to identify, characterise, and understand changes in Southern Ocean dynamics.  This position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge Antarctic research in an international, collaborative environment, with the possibility of participating in Antarctic research cruises. The successful candidate will work closely with collaborators at the British Antarctic Survey, University College London, the University of Gothenburg, the Norwegian Polar Institute and the University of Naples Parthenope.  We welcome applications from researchers with experience in physical oceanography, satellite remote sensing, ocean observations, numerical modelling, or related disciplines such as mathematics and physics.  The position is expected to start on 1 March 2027 for an initial period of two years, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory progress and funding availability. Some flexibility regarding the start date is available and can be discussed with the successful candidate. For further information or informal enquiries, please contact Dr Alessandro Silvano  a.silvano@soton.ac.uk . items.title: Research Fellow in Global Marine Ecosystem Modelling (3551126HN)
items.description:
We have an exciting opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to investigate how phytoplankton physiology influences ocean carbon cycling. The successful candidate will join a UK-US research project, From Monod to Macromolecules: assessing nutrient-carbon coupling in a hierarchy of ocean-ecosystem models, based at the University of Southampton and working in collaboration with researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).  The project will compare different approaches to representing phytoplankton physiology within the MITgcm-Darwin ocean ecosystem model. The successful candidate will implement and evaluate a range of physiological sub-models with the MIT virtual ocean environment, to investigate which aspects of cellular physiology are important for predicting nutrient cycling, primary production and carbon export.  The work will involve developing and testing numerical models, running global ocean simulations and analysing model outputs alongside oceanographic observations. There will also be opportunities to investigate how the effects of physiological complexity depend on environmental variability and ecological interactions.  We are looking for someone with strong quantitative and programming skills, and experience developing or analysing numerical models. A background in marine ecology, oceanography, biogeochemistry, applied mathematics or a related field would be beneficial. Experience with Fortran, high-performance computing and/or marine ecosystem models would be advantageous, but is not essential.  At Southampton, you will work closely with Dr Ben Ward and Professor Mark Moore, in collaboration with Professor Mick Follows, Dr Stephanie Dutkiewicz and colleagues at MIT. You will also have opportunities to work with staff and students across the wider Marine Biogeochemistry research group and the School of Ocean and Earth Science at the University of Southampton. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the publication of research findings in peer-reviewed journals and to present their work at national and international scientific conferences.  We welcome applications from all candidates with an interest in the role, and those who are committed to helping us create a diverse and inclusive work environment.  We encourage applications from candidates from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities, people who identify as LGBTQ+ and people with disabilities. We recognise that employees may wish to have working patterns that fit with their caring responsibilities or work-life balance.  Due consideration will be given to applicants who have had career breaks for reasons including maternity, paternity or adoption leave, disability or illness. We offer a generous holiday allowance and additional University closure days, subsidised health and fitness facilities and access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS).  Applications for Research Fellow positions will be considered from candidates who are working towards or nearing completion of a relevant PhD qualification.   The position is full-time and fixed-term for 20 months, with an anticipated start in early 2027.   For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Ben Ward ( b.a.ward@soton.ac.uk ). items.title: Research Fellow in Optical Communication Systems (3549526BA)
items.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated Research Fellow to work on novel technologies and applications of fibre communication systems.  Be a part of the University of Southampton, an institution in the top one per cent of world universities and one of the UK’s Russell group research-intensive universities. We have an international reputation for research, teaching and enterprise activities. You will work in the world leading Optoelectronics Research Centre (ORC) and will have access to the world class facilities and dedicated researchers that this provides. The Telecommunications Systems Laboratory is equipped with state-of-the-art equipment for experimentation in photonic systems and provides direct access to the UK’s National Dark Fibre Facility, a unique geographically distributed transmission facility dedicated to research, linking together four top British universities.  You will contribute to research projects that experimentally investigate communication systems using state-of-the-art optical technologies, including novel amplifiers, integrated photonic components, and hollow-core and multi-core optical fibres. Your research will explore the potential of these technologies in future communication systems. This will require an in-depth understanding of the physical characteristics of optical fibres and devices, and the ability to develop innovative ways to deploy them in network configurations. You will work closely with project partners and other researchers within the group and across the ORC.  To be successful, you must have a strong background in photonics and communications with extensive practical experience of working with optical fibres and systems. Ideally, you will also have experience in characterising optical fibres, photonic components, optical system modelling and/or the design and experimentation of high-speed optical communication systems.  You must also have proven skills in the critical evaluation and interpretation of data, reporting your findings succinctly and working as part of a collaborative research team. You must hold a PhD* or equivalent qualification related to fibre optics or photonics. Previous postdoctoral experience is favoured but not necessary. items.title: Research Fellow – 2D Ferroelectric Devices (3550026FP)
items.description:
You will join the  2D-MINDs  team, led by Dr Soumya Sarkar within the Sustainable Electronic Technologies research group in the School of Electronics and Computer Science (ECS) at the University of Southampton. You will also be part of the interdisciplinary  ECS Centre for Neuromorphic Technologies  (CeNT).  The position is funded by the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship  “2D semiconductors for intelligent non-volatile memory devices” (2DMINDs) . The post will be full-time for a period until 31/01/2029 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for another 12 months.   You will investigate two-dimensional semiconductors and ferroelectric materials to develop non-volatile memory that co-locates storage and processing for low-power AI hardware. Your research will combine materials characterisation, interface engineering and device fabrication at  Southampton Nanofabrication Centre  to develop foundry-compatible fabrication protocols alongside specialist electrical and optical characterisation facilities. Training and support will be provided to develop the skills required for your research.  The role is well suited to candidates who wish to develop their expertise in emerging memory devices and neuromorphic technologies within a supportive, interdisciplinary research environment. We welcome applicants with complementary experimental backgrounds; experience across all the areas listed below is not expected.  You should be a resourceful and passionate researcher who will plan and conduct experiments, develop measurement techniques and generate high-quality research data. You will contribute to the project’s scientific direction, prepare manuscripts, undertake short research visits to project partners (University of Cambridge, NPL), present findings at international conferences, write project reports and support the supervision of master’s and PhD students.  The role offers support for conference travel, collaboration, industry engagement and outreach. Extensive leadership training and transferable skills development will support your progression towards research independence and future leadership in ferroelectric neuromorphic devices.   Essential requirements    A PhD, or near completion of a PhD, in materials science, physics, electronic engineering or a related discipline.  Experience in one or more of the following: fabrication and characterisation of devices based on 2D semiconductors, or ferroelectric materials.  Strong experimental and analytical skills, with the ability to plan research, interpret results and solve technical problems.  Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams.    Desirable experience    Ferroelectric transistors, tunnel junctions or diodes, or other non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices.  E-beam lithography, thin-film deposition or dry-transfer assembly of van der Waals heterostructures.  Temperature-dependent electrical transport or pulsed electrical measurements.  Optical spectroscopy, including Raman, photoluminescence or reflectance, or scanning probe microscopy, including AFM, PFM or KPFM.  Contributing to academic publications, collaborative research or student supervision.   We warmly welcome applicants from all backgrounds, particularly those underrepresented in the field. ECS holds an Athena SWAN Silver award in recognition of its continued commitment to improving equality for women in science and engineering. We have a range of staff development programmes and a unique mentoring and wellbeing scheme. We recognise that research careers follow different paths and welcome applications from candidates whose PhD completion or career progression has been affected by caring responsibilities, health conditions or other personal circumstances. International applicants are encouraged to apply. Informal enquiries should be directed to Dr Soumya Sarkar ( soumya.sarkar@soton.ac.uk ).   Apply by uploading your  CV  and a  cover letter  detailing how your skills and experience match the requirements of the role.

Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate why individuals with similar levels of adiposity differ substantially in their risk of developing type 2 diabetes and its complications. Working alongside genetic epidemiologists, clinicians and data scientists, you will apply statistical genetics approaches, including genome-wide association studies (GWAS), Mendelian randomisation and post-GWAS analyses, to identify genetic determinants, investigate causal relationships and uncover biological pathways linking obesity to metabolic disease.   As a Research Fellow, you will:     Investigate the genetic and biological heterogeneity of obesity and its relationships with type 2 diabetes and related complications.  Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of obesity-related traits, adiposity phenotypes and metabolic outcomes using large-scale genetic and epidemiological datasets.  Apply Mendelian randomisation and complementary genetic epidemiological approaches to investigate potential causal relationships between different aspects of adiposity, type 2 diabetes and its complications.  Perform post-GWAS analyses, including fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation and pathway enrichment, to identify genes and biological mechanisms underlying obesity-related metabolic risk.  Investigate the genetic determinants of different obesity-related phenotypes and their associations with metabolic and cardiometabolic outcomes.  Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings. Knowledge of post-GWAS approaches, such as fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation, colocalisation or pathway analyses.  An understanding of genetic epidemiology and statistical methods used to investigate the genetic architecture and biological mechanisms of complex diseases.  Evidence of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications.  Excellent analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams.   Experience in obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiometabolic disease research or the genetic analysis of adiposity-related traits would be advantageous.    At Southampton, you will join a supportive, internationally connected research environment at the forefront of genetic epidemiology, data science and metabolic disease research.    We offer:     Access to large-scale genetic and biomedical datasets, high-performance computing infrastructure and secure analytical environments.  Opportunities to investigate the genetic and biological mechanisms underlying obesity heterogeneity, type 2 diabetes and its complications. items.title: Research Fellow in Cell and Developmental Biology (3545826BJ)
items.description:
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Research Fellow to join the Salah Elias laboratory at the University of Southampton and lead the experimental research within a BBSRC-funded project investigating mechanisms of mammary epithelial morphogenesis through AI-integrated human organoid models and predictive cell fate mapping. This is an excellent opportunity to shape an innovative project and develop a distinctive interdisciplinary profile at the interface of cell and developmental biology, human organoid models, advanced imaging, molecular phenotyping and computational biology.   About the project   The project combines patient-derived mammary organoids, high-resolution 3D/4D imaging, single-cell transcriptomics and AI-driven analysis and modelling to uncover mechanisms governing epithelial morphogenesis. At its core is a fundamental question: how do polarised cell divisions coordinate luminogenesis with cell fate and differentiation to build and maintain functional epithelial architecture? By addressing this question in physiologically relevant human models, the project aims to define how these mechanisms safeguard epithelial integrity and how their disruption leads to abnormal tissue organisation.  You will take a central role in the scientific development of this ambitious programme, including experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. You will use patient-derived human mammary organoids and gene loss-of-function approaches, together with high-resolution 3D/4D fluorescence imaging, fate mapping, advanced quantitative analysis, and single-cell RNA sequencing, to connect molecular and cellular mechanisms with cell fate and tissue architecture.  A major strength of the project is the integration of experimental and computational biology. Working with computational researchers, you will integrate multimodal imaging and transcriptomic data into AI-driven mechanistic and predictive models to determine how changes at the level of individual cells influence tissue-level organisation and function. You will have strong experimental experience across several relevant areas of cell and developmental biology, which may include organoid or mammalian cell culture, epithelial biology, high-resolution fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology. An understanding of computational or mathematical modelling would be advantageous, but is not essential. You should be able to plan and conduct rigorous experiments, interpret data, troubleshoot methods and communicate findings clearly.  Alongside leading the experimental research, you will contribute scientific ideas and interpretation, support collaborative projects, help develop grant proposals, prepare research for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, train colleagues in new methods and advise on scientific protocols. You will bring excellent interpersonal skills and work constructively with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines. You will have access to state-of-the-art microscopy, flow-cytometry and high-performance computing facilities, multidisciplinary training and career-development opportunities. items.title: Research Fellow in Geo-Foundation Models (ENVGE1288)
items.description:
Are you excited by the potential of foundation models to transform how we understand places and the people who move through them? Would you like to help build a new generation of geographic models grounded in how people actually perceive and remember cities? Do you enjoy working at the boundary between machine learning and real-world application?   ReCoGNiSe (Representations of Cognitive Geography for Navigating Sustainable Neighbourhoods) is a five-year, €2m research programme funded by a European Research Council Consolidator Grant. ReCoGNiSe starts from a critical disconnect at the heart of geographic analysis: that the digital representations of space on which spatial data are built do not reflect how places are perceived and remembered. The project aims to initiate a step-change in how geographic space is represented, building new representations of spatial features and relations, grounded in spatial cognition and computational neuroscience.  We are looking to recruit a passionate researcher to lead our work on cognitive feature representations using foundation models. You will use a vast array of data to build rich, multimodal representations of urban cognitive features, capturing facets such as visual salience, cultural significance, function, and locational importance. This will involve working with general-purpose language, vision-language and multimodal models, alongside geospatial foundation models. Your representations will provide the foundation for the project's cognitive map representations. Working with the wider project team, you will adapt approaches to reflect newly collected data on how features are perceived differently across populations and over time, and integrate with other work on constructing models of spatial learning. They will also underpin the project's open-source releases.  Candidates will require expertise in deep learning and foundation models, ideally applied to geospatial or human-generated data. Given this work sits at the interface of GeoAI, geography and neuroscience, we are particularly seeking applicants who enjoy working across disciplinary boundaries, are committed to open and responsible AI, and are keen to engage with theory from geography and spatial cognition.  This role will be hosted within the  Mobility Science Lab , in the Institute for Spatial Data Science (ISDS) at the School of Geography. As well as working closely with Prof Ed Manley and the wider ReCoGNiSe research team (totalling three Research Fellows and two PhD students), you will collaborate with Dr Weiming Huang (University of Leeds), who brings expertise in foundation models and GeoAI, and Prof Hugo Spiers (UCL), who brings expertise in the neuroscience of spatial cognition. You will also benefit from the project's international network of collaborators in spatial cognition, GeoAI and urban science. items.description:
Overview of the Role   Are you a researcher with demonstrable expertise in the analysis of climatological data and the implementation and interpretation of climate model projections? Do you have a demonstrable interest in engaging with stakeholders, particularly in public policy and the financial sector? Do you have a background within climate science?    This project will address the lack of adequate early-warning systems for accelerated climate change and tipping-points, for the insurance sector and more broadly. It also aims to address an associated challenge for the insurance sector, given its criticality to the global economy, by helping the sector understand the stressors, and adaptation responses to those stressors, it is likely to face in the coming decades due to the combined effects of climate change, the transition to a net zero economy including regulatory challenges, and potential geopolitical threats.  Through this work, in collaboration with the insurance and reinsurance industry, the successful candidate will help to develop and test a novel early-warning system for accelerating climate change and tipping-points, with aim of informing policy and wider society that unmanageable levels of climate change, with different modalities of climate impacts, are approaching.  This approach draws on ideas from climate attribution and optimal fingerprinting and from economics signal detection but extends this through the application of social science techniques, including decision-gaming and reverse stress testing, by using the insurance sector as a filter to help detect the early signs of an accelerated climate change signal against the background noise of natural variability in the climate. Build the next stage of your research career at Leeds   Are you an outstanding postdoctoral researcher with ambitions to become an independent adult social care researcher? Do you have important research questions you want to lead and develop?   If so, we want to hear from you .  This fellowship provides the opportunity to develop and deliver  your own programme of adult social care research  within the School of Healthcare at the University of Leeds. You will be hosted within Nurturing Innovation in Care Home Excellence in Leeds (NICHE-Leeds) and connected to the wider research community across the University of Leeds, Leeds Beckett University and the NIHR School for Social Care Research (SSCR).  The fellowship offers protected research time, mentorship and career development support. Up to  £30,000 is available to support research activity, training and career development .   Research that matters   Our research addresses major challenges facing adult social care and seeks to improve the lives of people who draw on care and support, their families and carers, and the social care workforce. Our strengths include research on the workforce, technology and digital innovation, dementia, older people, care homes, quality and safety, implementation science, and knowledge mobilisation.  We particularly welcome researchers who will extend, challenge or complement our existing strengths, bringing new questions, theoretical perspectives, methodologies or disciplines to adult social care.   Work where research and social care meet   You will work within NICHE-Leeds, a partnership between social care and academia. NICHE-Leeds brings together researchers, people drawing on social care, families, care staff, providers and other partners to identify priorities, generate evidence and support its use in practice.You will benefit from our membership of NIHR SSCR, providing access to training, networking and career development opportunities. Successful Fellows also become NIHR Academy Members.   Who we are looking for   You will have a PhD in a discipline relevant to adult social care research and a developing track record demonstrating the potential to become an independent social care researcher.  We are particularly interested in applicants who can demonstrate:  •      intellectual ambition and originality;  •      a strong commitment to adult social care research;  •      excellent research and methodological capability;  •      potential to develop a distinctive programme of research;  •      ability to collaborate across disciplinary and organisational boundaries; and  •      commitment to research that matters for people, services, policy and practice.   As part of the application, you will need to outline the research you want to develop, describe your methodological, substantive and career development plans, and how Leeds will support your progression.
